title: Physics-Inspired Visual AI
subtitle: Grounding Foundation, Generative, and World Models in Physical Principles
overview: Visual foundation models, vision-language models, diffusion models, and world models have expanded what computer vision can do. Without explicit models of image formation and scene physics, their outputs can look convincing while violating physical constraints, failing across sensors, or hiding uncertainty in inverse problems.
scope: The special issue welcomes research that uses physical priors to improve visual perception and generation, or applies pretrained and generative models to reconstruction, rendering, restoration, and computational imaging. The scope spans theory, methods, empirical studies, and benchmarks that advance computer vision.

topics.title: Physics-grounded foundation models
topics.description: Use priors from image formation, geometry, illumination, materials, and sensors to train, adapt, and evaluate visual and vision-language foundation models and improve their reasoning.

topics.title: Physics-consistent generative models
topics.description: Apply physical constraints to diffusion models and AI-generated content, including controllable generation, inverse rendering, relighting, and restoration.

topics.title: Physics-aware world models & embodied AI
topics.description: Build interactive environments that respond to actions and test perception under controlled physical conditions.

topics.title: Physics-constrained data & sensors
topics.description: Acquire, simulate, augment, and enhance data while preserving physical properties. Relevant modalities include spectral, event, light-field, time-of-flight, and LiDAR sensing.

topics.title: Evaluation, benchmarks & applications
topics.description: Measure physical consistency and uncertainty, diagnose hallucinations, and assess performance in adverse weather, material recognition, and real deployments.
